answer.ruling: Rule compares each player's warriors plus buildings; tokens and pawns do not count. Ordinary ties mean nobody rules. Eyrie win ties for most if they have at least one Eyrie piece there. Vagabond cannot rule or stop another player ruling.
answer.evidence: Shared movement, crafting and battle — Rule (2.5)

answers.evidence: Shared movement, crafting and battle — Rule (2.5)

answer.ruling: Move any positive number of your warriors/pawns from one clearing along a linking path to an adjacent clearing; rule origin or destination or both, rechecking for each move. The same pieces may move repeatedly, including multiple moves in one action. Rivers are not paths unless an effect explicitly treats them as paths.
answer.evidence: Shared movement, crafting and battle — Move (4.2)

answers.evidence: Shared movement, crafting and battle — Move (4.2)

answer.ruling: Choose a clearing containing your warriors/pawn and an enemy as defender; you need not rule it. Defender may play matching ambush (birds wild); attacker may foil with matching ambush, which discards the defender's card and prevents hits. Otherwise ambush deals two immediate hits, then is discarded; battle ends if no attacking warriors/pawns remain. Resolve before-roll effects (attacker orders effects if both sides have them), roll: high die attacker, low die defender, equal dice equal hits; rolled hits capped by own warriors in battle (Alliance defending reverses dice; Vagabond uses undamaged swords). Resolve after-roll effects with attacker choosing order; count extra hits uncapped and subtract ignored hits; defenseless adds one attacker hit if defender has no warriors (Vagabond instead if no undamaged swords). Each hit removes an opposing piece; hit recipient chooses removal order but all warriors before buildings/tokens, and their removal-triggered effects order. Both sides deal counted hits; warrior losses do not recalculate cap. Each removed enemy building/token scores one VP to whoever removes it, attacking or defending.
answer.evidence: Shared movement, crafting and battle — Battle (4.3)

answers.evidence: Shared movement, crafting and battle — Battle (4.3)

answer.part: crafting costs, reuse, supply, duplicate effects
answer.ruling: Use bottom-left crafting icons, not card suit. For each icon Marquise activates a matching-suit workshop, Eyrie a matching roost, Alliance matching sympathy; each piece can activate once per turn. Vagabond exhausts one face-up undamaged hammer per icon, may reuse the pawn, and current clearing must match every icon (one clearing cannot pay mixed suits). Three-color question-mark accepts any suit. An item card cannot be crafted if its matching map supply token is absent. An identical persistent effect already in play cannot be crafted again.
answer.evidence: Shared movement, crafting and battle — Craft (4.1)

answers.evidence: Shared movement, crafting and battle — Craft (4.1)

answer.ruling: In your Daylight at 10 or more VP, activate a dominance card from hand into play, remove your score marker and stop scoring VP. At start of your Birdsong, win by ruling three clearings of the dominance's matching mouse/rabbit/fox suit, or for bird dominance ruling two diagonally opposite corner clearings. Earlier fulfillment does not win immediately. An activated dominance cannot be removed or replaced.

answer.part: spent dominance and taking an available card
answer.ruling: A dominance card that would enter discard instead goes near the map as available. During your Daylight, spend a matching card to take an available dominance into hand. Available bird dominance remains bird, so it requires a bird payment; a bird card can pay for a non-bird dominance. Taking it does not activate it.

In setup, randomly determine starting player and seating, choose factions and map, and put scores at zero. With two players remove all four dominance cards; shuffle shared deck and each player draws three cards. Cover four R slots with ruins. Map item supply is 2 boots, 2 bags, 1 crossbow, 1 hammer, 2 swords, 2 tea, 2 coins. Only if Vagabond is present, during its setup hide one R-marked bag, boot, hammer, sword under each of four ruins, shuffle stacks and return to empty R slots; without Vagabond ruins contain no items. Set factions up in letter order Marquise, Eyrie, Alliance, Vagabond; this is distinct from turn order.
answer.evidence: Setup — Standard Setup and Hidden ruin items

answers.evidence: Setup — Standard Setup and Hidden ruin items

answer.ruling: Only Marquise may place pieces in the Keep clearing; others may move pieces into it. Whenever any number of Marquise warriors are removed from a clearing, Marquise may spend one card matching that clearing to put those warriors in the Keep clearing instead of supply, including removals outside battle. Without a Keep there is no hospital destination. The Keep cannot be placed again once removed.

Craft with workshops first, then take up to three actions plus one per bird card spent outside an action, in any order/number subject to Recruit's once-per-turn limit. March is up to two moves, and the compound action cannot be interrupted to spend a bird or take another action. Recruit places one warrior at each recruiter, only once per turn. Overwork spends a card matching a sawmill's clearing to place one wood there.

Choose a clearing you rule with an open building slot and choose a building type. Take that type's leftmost building from its track. Pay the full cost shown atop its column in wood from the target clearing or other ruled clearings connected to it through an unbroken chain of ruled clearings. Place the building and score VP shown on the newly uncovered track space. Requires full wood cost, available building and legal slot.
answer.evidence: Marquise de Cat — Daylight, Build; Player Reference

answers.evidence: Marquise de Cat — Daylight, Build; Player Reference

answer.ruling: In order: Emergency Orders draws one card if hand is empty; Add to Decree must add one or two hand cards, at most one bird, to any columns; A New Roost applies only if no roosts are on map and places one roost plus three warriors in a clearing with the fewest warriors where all those pieces can be placed.

Craft with roosts first, then resolve every card column by column Recruit, Move, Battle, Build; choose order within a column. Recruit card suit matches a roost clearing and places one warrior at one chosen roost there (Charismatic places two). Move suit matches origin and must move at least one warrior under normal path/rule requirements. Battle suit matches battle clearing and initiates battle with Eyrie warriors and enemy. Build suit matches target, where Eyrie rules, slot is open and no roost is already present; place a roost. Bird cards are wild but still meet action requirements. Any required action not fully completable causes immediate Turmoil; cannot skip or proceed.

Lose one VP per bird Decree card, including both Loyal Viziers; discard every Decree card except Viziers; flip current leader face down and choose a face-up replacement (if none, flip all leaders face up first); retuck Viziers in the replacement's columns. Daylight ends. Continue the full normal Evening: score roost track, draw one plus uncovered bonuses, discard to five. Turmoil does not remove map warriors or buildings.

When another player removes sympathy or moves any warriors into a sympathetic clearing, that player adds one matching hand card (birds count) per affected move, not per warrior; removing sympathy also triggers. If no matching card including birds, show hand to Alliance, which draws one deck card into Supporters. With full Supporters, discard incoming card but payment/no-match draw still occurs. Mere battle without sympathy removal, placing warriors there, or moving only Vagabond pawn does not trigger.

Both happen in Birdsong; do any number, but finish all Revolts before any Spread Sympathy. Each supporter spent for either action must match target clearing; birds wild. Revolt: choose sympathetic clearing without base, matching a base still on board; spend two matching supporters; remove all enemy pieces there, score one VP per enemy building/token, place matching base, then warriors there equal to matching-suit sympathetic clearings including that clearing and one warrior in Officers. Spread: choose unsympathetic clearing adjacent by path to sympathy, or any clearing if none; spend supporter cost shown above next token, plus one matching supporter for Martial Law if one other player has at least three warriors there; place sympathy and score uncovered VP. Only one sympathy per clearing; Keep placement ban applies. Cannot revolt in a newly sympathetically spread clearing that same Birdsong.

Train during Daylight by spending a hand card matching a clearing with a base to place one supply warrior in Officers; Supporters cannot pay. Organize is an Evening operation: remove one Alliance warrior from an unsympathetic clearing, place sympathy there and score uncovered VP; no supporter, adjacency or Martial Law cost, but token placement must be legal. Each officer permits one Evening operation; officers are not consumed. On base loss, discard all supporters matching that clearing including birds, remove half officers rounded up, and if no bases remain discard supporters above five.

answers.evidence: Woodland Alliance — Losing a base; Daylight; Evening

answer.part: Vagabond Refresh, Slip, Move, Rest and Evening draw
answer.ruling: Birdsong Refresh: count tea already face up on Refresh track; flip two exhausted items per such tea, then three more; tea refreshed now adds no refresh. Optional Slip moves to adjacent clearing/forest without boots, even into hostile warriors, ignoring effects preventing movement out; forest adjacency is per summary (touching clearing without crossing printed path; forests separated by one path; Winter river also divides forests). Daylight Move exhausts one boot plus one extra if destination has warriors of any Hostile faction; ignores rule, cannot enter forest, and from forest can move only to adjacent clearing. Evening in forest returns damaged items to Satchel face up and moves ready tea/coins/bags onto tracks if able; this does not refresh undamaged exhausted items. Always draw one card plus one per face-up coin on track, even after Rest, then discard to five and check capacity.

Explore exhausts torch in ruin clearing, takes one hidden item face up into Satchel/track and scores one VP if item taken; taking last item removes ruin and frees slot. Quest in matching clearing exhausts its two listed items, completes quest, chooses VP equal to matching completed quests including this one or draws two cards, then draws replacement quest; no cards pay. Repair exhausts hammer and moves one damaged item to Satchel retaining its face; ready tea/coins/bags move to tracks if room.

Removing one warrior of a non-Hostile faction immediately makes it Hostile (except allied-warrior battle-loss special case). On Vagabond's own-turn battle, Infamy gives one extra VP per hostile piece removed except the warrior that first caused Hostile status; no Infamy on others' turns or Strike. Aid cannot reduce Hostility, though can still obtain a crafted item. Strike exhausts crossbow to remove one enemy warrior; only if that faction has no warriors there may it remove another faction piece; check hostility. Strike gives no Infamy.

Vagabond cannot activate normal dominance. With four or more players, during own Daylight at 10+ VP activate dominance to coalition with a player not already in coalition whose VP is lowest among players other than Vagabond (choose among ties); put score marker on partner board and stop scoring. If partner wins, Vagabond also wins, including partner's dominance win. Coalition partner is not an enemy; if Hostile, marker resets to Indifferent; coalition alone grants no Allied powers.

Card overrides Law, Law overrides Learning to Play; when general and faction rules conflict, faction rule wins. “Cannot” is absolute unless explicitly overridden, so an ordinary card cannot override it absent explicit override.

If simultaneous effects have no clear order or decision maker, the player taking the turn chooses. A Marquise March's two moves are one compound action and cannot be interrupted to spend a bird card or take another action.

At-start effects precede all other effects of that phase; at-end effects follow everything else in that phase before next phase. Once the last step of a turn begins, no other actions are allowed except explicitly end-of-Evening/turn actions.

Hand size is public, contents private; reveal/show only when explicitly instructed. Face-up piles can be searched/inspected; deck cannot. Agreements are non-binding; cards transfer only as instructed, and actions require no consent.
answer.evidence: Special Rules & Edge Cases — Cards and information

answers.evidence: Special Rules & Edge Cases — Cards and information

answer.ruling: When shared deck empties, immediately shuffle discard into new deck. Birds substitute for any non-bird suit, including multiple same-suit payments. When instructed to give/discard non-bird suit cards, treat birds as that suit in the required quantity. A non-bird cannot substitute for an explicitly bird cost.

Pieces are finite; no proxies. If instructed to place more pieces than remain, place maximum possible and cannot voluntarily place fewer. Shortage does not waive costs or prerequisites, and does not excuse Eyrie's obligation to fully complete Decree actions; failure to complete causes Turmoil.
answer.evidence: Shared movement, crafting and battle — finite pieces; Eyrie Decree

answers.evidence: Shared movement, crafting and battle — finite pieces; Eyrie Decree

answer.ruling: Placement normally uses supply or leftmost track piece; removal returns pieces to supply or tracked pieces to rightmost empty track space. Removed items leave game permanently. For simultaneous removal, remove all pieces before triggering removal effects.
answer.evidence: Shared movement, crafting and battle — removal and placement

answers.evidence: Shared movement, crafting and battle — removal and placement

answer.ruling: Resolve forced action as if affected player chose it, retaining that player's abilities and restrictions. A player forced to battle makes its battle decisions.
Replace requires both removal and placement to be possible; the Keep placement ban cannot be bypassed by replacing an enemy piece there. Swap ignores move/place restrictions, unlike move or place.
If multiple players reach 30 simultaneously, tied player closest clockwise to current player wins, including current player.

Forest is enclosed by printed paths and clearings; adjacent to clearings touching it without crossing a printed path and to forests separated by just one printed path. Winter river also divides forests as paths do. Fall has no special rules.

Supply 25 warriors and 8 wood. Put Keep in any corner starting clearing; put one warrior in every clearing except diagonally opposite corner. Place one sawmill, workshop and recruiter among Keep clearing and adjacent clearings in any combination respecting slots. Put remaining five of each building type on tracks right-to-left, leaving leftmost space empty.

Supply 20 warriors. Put one roost and six warriors in a corner that is not another player's starting corner, diagonally opposite a starting corner if possible. Choose leader and keep others face up; tuck two bird Loyal Viziers in leader's listed columns. Fill roost track with other six roosts from right to left.

Supply 10 warriors; put three bases in matching board spaces and ten sympathy on its track. Draw three additional cards face down into Supporters, separate from three-card hand. Start with no map pieces or officers.

Choose Thief, Tinker or Ranger; put pawn in any forest; shuffle quests and display three face up. Take character's S-marked starting items: tea, coins, bags face up on matching tracks, other items face up in Satchel; return unused S items to box. Set every other faction relationship marker to Indifferent.
Recommended minimum Reach: 17 for two players, 18 for three, 21 for four. Faction values: Marquise 10, Eyrie 7, Vagabond 5, Alliance 3. Adventurous groups may use any mix totaling at least 17.

Birdsong places one wood per sawmill (one per sawmill if multiple there), limited by shared finite supply of eight. Each Daylight Overwork spends a card matching sawmill clearing to place one wood there, from same supply. Evening draw one card plus one per uncovered draw bonus, then discard to five.
answer.evidence: Marquise de Cat — Wood production, Birdsong, Evening

answers.evidence: Marquise de Cat — Wood production, Birdsong, Evening

answer.ruling: Recruit once per turn: one warrior at each recruiter. If supply cannot fill all, place maximum available, choosing among eligible recruiters.
Eyrie crafted items score one VP rather than printed VP under Disdain for Trade; other extra crafting-point effects still apply. Builder ignores Disdain and thus is not subject to that reduction.

Builder: Viziers Recruit/Move; ignores Disdain. Charismatic: Recruit/Battle; each Recruit places two warriors. Commander: Move/Battle; one extra hit as attacker. Despot: Move/Build; when battle removes at least one enemy building/token, score one extra VP in addition to normal removal points.

Charismatic Recruit must place two warriors at one chosen roost. Decree actions must be fully completed; if only one warrior remains, it cannot fulfill the two-warrior requirement and Eyrie immediately enters Turmoil.

answers.evidence: Eyrie Dynasties — Decree Recruit; Turmoil; finite pieces

answer.ruling: Alliance defending reverses dice assignment: Alliance uses higher die and attacker lower. Warrior caps still apply to rolled hits.
Alliance may inspect Supporters; stack is face down and separate. Supporters can only be spent for suit, not crafting; they are not hand cards and do not count toward five-card hand limit.
No. All Revolts must be completed before starting any Spread Sympathy; cannot return to Revolt once spreading begins, so new sympathy cannot support a same-Birdsong Revolt.

Two different enemy players with two warriors each do not meet Martial Law: chosen clearing needs at least three warriors of one other player. Martial Law adds one matching supporter for Spread Sympathy. Organize has no Martial Law cost.

Placing warriors in sympathy does not trigger Outrage; moving only Vagabond pawn does not trigger. Moving warriors into sympathy triggers it, including allied warriors accompanying Vagabond; the mover adds one matching hand card per affected move, not per warrior, or follows no-match rule.

Operations are Move, Battle, Recruit, Organize, up to number of officers, any order/repetition; officers are not consumed. Recruit places one warrior at one clearing with a base. After operations, draw one plus uncovered draw bonuses, then discard to five.
Pawn cannot be removed. If an enemy effect removes all enemy pieces from its clearing, Vagabond instead damages three items.

Vagabond's rolled hit maximum is all undamaged swords in Satchel, face up or down; exhausted undamaged swords count. Defenseless only if no undamaged swords. Hits damage one undamaged item each; excess hits are ignored if none remain.
answer.evidence: Battle; Vagabond — Daylight Battle, Pawn and items

answers.evidence: Battle; Vagabond — Daylight Battle, Pawn and items

answer.ruling: Face-up tea/coins/bags in Satchel immediately move to empty matching track spaces if possible; each track holds at most three. Exhausting track item sends it to Satchel. Damaging item enters Damaged box with face unchanged. Actions require face-up undamaged items; damaged items cannot pay. Track item exhausted can be in Satchel after exhaustion; refreshing changes face, not damage.

Satchel plus Damaged box capacity is six plus two per face-up bag on track; track items do not count. At Evening's final capacity step, permanently remove chosen Satchel/Damaged items until within limit. No check immediately on acquiring items.

Forest Rest returns all damaged items to Satchel and flips them face up; ready tea/coins/bags go to tracks if possible. It does not refresh undamaged exhausted items. Refresh flips exhausted items according to tea count plus three, changing face not damage; Repair exhausts hammer to move one damaged item to Satchel, retaining its face.

answers.evidence: Vagabond — Birdsong Refresh; Daylight Repair; Evening

answer.ruling: Exhaust one face-up undamaged item of any type and give a card matching current clearing to player with faction pieces there, even if Hostile. May take one item from their Crafted Items into Satchel/track, but an available item is not required to Aid. Advancement requires the printed number of Aid actions to same non-Hostile faction in same turn; each Aid counts for only one improvement. Score VP printed in new relationship space; Hostile cannot advance.

At Allied, each subsequent Aid scores two VP. Vagabond may move warriors of one Allied faction along with pawn to destination, subject to their movement restrictions; moving into sympathy triggers Outrage. At start of battle as attacker, may treat one Allied faction's warriors there as own, adding them to all undamaged swords for maximum rolled hits; may attack another enemy, not that ally itself.

In battle using allied warriors as own, may absorb hits by removing those warriors or damaging items. If more allied warriors removed than items damaged in that battle, that ally becomes Hostile at battle end; equal counts do not trigger it. This overrides ordinary hostility timing for these friendly losses.

answer.part: crafting mixed icons, reuse, use item
answer.ruling: Vagabond cannot craft fox-and-rabbit cost from one clearing, because current clearing must match every icon. Pawn may activate repeatedly, but exhaust one face-up undamaged hammer per icon each time. A crafted item may immediately be taken face up into Satchel/track and used for another Daylight action immediately if requirements are met.

Thief starts boot, torch, tea, sword; Steal exhausts torch to take random hand card from player with faction pieces in clearing. Tinker starts boot, torch, bag, hammer; Day Labor exhausts torch to take discard-pile card matching clearing (bird always qualifies). Ranger starts boot, torch, crossbow, sword; Hideout exhausts torch to repair three items retaining faces, immediately ends Daylight and begins Evening.
Taking the last hidden item removes ruin and frees building slot. Ruins can be removed only when explicitly allowed; ordinary building placement does not authorize removing a ruin.
Coalition partners are not enemies, so cannot be attacked as an enemy. Coalition does not by itself grant Allied relationship powers.

The first warrior removed makes that faction Hostile, and that warrior earns no Infamy; the second hostile warrior earns 1 Infamy VP and no ordinary removal VP. The building earns 1 ordinary removal VP plus 1 Infamy VP. Total: 3 VP (1 ordinary building + 2 eligible hostile pieces Infamy).
answer.evidence: Vagabond — Hostile/Infamy; Scoring — Ordinary removal VP

answers.evidence: Vagabond — Hostile/Infamy; Scoring — Ordinary removal VP

answer.ruling: Into a clearing with hostile buildings/tokens but no hostile warriors: one boot. Into a clearing with hostile warriors, including warriors of several Hostile factions: one boot plus one extra boot, total two; extra is per destination condition, not per faction.
Taking an available dominance puts it in hand; does not activate. Activation is separate. Taking and activating are Daylight procedures and neither requires a Marquise action allowance.

Faction-piece ownership cannot change; each player owns their chosen faction and its listed faction pieces, except items. Items are not faction pieces; possessing an item does not make it faction-owned.

Immediate-effect crafting card resolves and is discarded to shared discard. Persistent-effect card stays in play area. A card in play is outside hand and cannot be spent, discarded or used for another purpose unless explicitly instructed.

Neither Ambush nor Dominance cards can be crafted. Defender may play matching Ambush for two immediate hits; attacker may play matching Ambush to foil defending Ambush. Dominance may be activated to change win condition or spent for suit.

Choose factions; randomly determine starting player and seating; take faction boards/pieces and map. Put score markers at zero. Distribute overview cards as desired and place battle dice nearby. Set factions up in letter order Marquise, Eyrie, Alliance, Vagabond; setup order is distinct from turn order.
First player to 30 VP wins immediately, on any player's turn; no need to finish action, phase or turn.
To initiate ordinary battle choose clearing with your warriors or pawn and an enemy there as defender. You do not need to rule the clearing.

Attacker chooses order of applicable before-roll effects when both players have them, and likewise after-roll effects. The side taking hits chooses order of effects triggered by its own pieces' removal.
In Count Hits, add extra hits (not capped by warriors) and subtract hits ignored by effects; defenseless adds one attacker hit in stated conditions.

The item token comes from map item supply and goes into crafting faction's Crafted Items box; that faction scores printed VP on crafting card subject to Eyrie's Disdain exception. Ordinary faction does not exhaust crafted item.

Eyrie activates roosts; Alliance activates sympathy. For each icon use a piece in a clearing matching that icon's suit; crafting piece suit is its clearing's suit. Three-color question-mark icon accepts any suit.

Mobilize adds one hand card to Supporters; without base keep at most five and discard overflow, with a base unlimited. Daylight Craft, Mobilize and Train can be done in any order and number, so no need to finish crafting first.
Score VP on rightmost empty roost-track space, then draw one plus uncovered draw bonuses and discard to five. This normal Evening occurs even after Turmoil.
To initiate Daylight Battle, exhaust one sword. An exhausted sword cannot pay because actions require a face-up undamaged item; although face-down undamaged swords count toward rolled-hit maximum.

answer.ruling: Turn phases are Birdsong, Daylight, Evening. Players take turns clockwise; after a player's Evening, the next clockwise player takes their turn.

Each Vagabond hit damages one undamaged item of Vagabond's choice, moving it to Damaged box without changing face. Already damaged items cannot take another hit; excess hits are ignored when no undamaged items remain.
Alliance may take up to its number of officers in Evening military operations, in any order/repetition. One Recruit operation places one warrior at one clearing with a base.
Vagabond may take item actions in any order and number as ready undamaged items permit; action types need no fixed order and may repeat, subject to each action's costs and requirements.

Strike exhausts one crossbow to remove one enemy warrior in clearing. Only if that enemy faction has no warriors there may you remove another piece of its faction instead. Exhausted or damaged crossbow cannot pay because actions require face-up undamaged items.
